research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0003/response.json:154:  "note_markdown": "# Weighted resultants and vertical separability over the prime field\n\n## Abstract\n\nFix a prime $p$, dimension $m=2$, and an integer $100<d<p$. I prove a prime-field refinement of the algebraic cleanup following weighted interpolation. If a squarefree $(1,1,d)$-weighted interpolant has weighted degree $D<p$, then after removing its content in $Z$, the primitive factor $B$ is automatically separable in $Z$: $\\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. Moreover, a weighted resultant calculation bounds the number of line-polynomial graphs on which both $B$ and $B_Z$ vanish identically by\n\n$$\n(2r-1)\\delta-dr^2\\le \\frac{\\delta^2}{d}-\\delta,\n$$\n\nwhere $\\delta=\\operatorname{wdeg}B$ and $r=\\deg_ZB$. Including content-trivial lines, at most $D^2/d-D$ lines must be discarded. Every other line has at most $D-d$ ramified points. This replaces the ordinary-degree bounds $D(D-1)$ and $D$ in KTZ by factor-$d$ sharper line control and the smaller point bound $D-d$.\n\nThe improvement is genuine but does not improve soundness. KTZ interpolation has $D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\varepsilon})$; the remaining $(D-d)/p$ loss is $O(\\sqrt{(d/p)/\\varepsilon})$. Making it $O(\\varepsilon)$ still requires $\\varepsilon^3\\gtrsim d/p$. Thus `benchmark_improved=false`.\n\nI also prove that the usual uniform ambient-multiplicity modification cannot change this exponent by raw coefficient counting, and give an explicit $p=409,d=101$ counterexample showing that a nonzero higher Hasse derivative cannot replace the simple-root hypothesis in Newton lifting.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nThere are $p(p+1)$ affine lines in $\\mathbb F_p^2$. The sampling model is exactly\n\n$$\nL\\sim\\operatorname{Unif}(\\mathcal L),\\qquad x\\sim\\operatorname{Unif}(L).\n$$\n\nFor a point table $f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p$ and supplied line polynomials $P_L$ of degree at most $d$, write\n\n$$\n\\varepsilon=\\Pr_{L,x\\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)].\n$$\n\nAll polynomial degrees below are formal degrees. The weights are\n\n$$\n\\operatorname{wt}(X)=\\operatorname{wt}(Y)=1,\\qquad \\operatorname{wt}(Z)=d.\n$$\n\nThus, if $A$ has weighted degree at most $D$ and $\\deg P_L\\le d$, then\n\n$$\n\\deg_t A(L(t),P_L(t))\\le D.\n$$\n\nFor the interpolation space set\n\n$$\nN_d(D)=\\sum_{k=0}^{\\lfloor D/d\\rfloor}\\binom{D-dk+2}{2}.\n$$\n\nThis is the exact number of monomials of weighted degree at most $D$. When $D<p$, every positive possible $Z$-exponent is below $p$, so ordinary $Z$-differentiation kills no such monomial merely because of the characteristic.\n\nIn the KTZ application, $\\mathcal R$ is the selected line family, $n=|\\mathcal R|$,\n\n$$\nk_0=\\left\\lfloor\\frac{\\varepsilon p}{100}\\right\\rfloor,\n\\quad\nk_1=\\left\\lfloor\\frac{\\varepsilon p}{1000}\\right\\rfloor,\n\\quad\nD=16(\\lfloor\\sqrt{dn}\\rfloor+1).\n$$\n\nTheir Lemmas 3.2 and 4.1 give\n\n$$\n100p\\le n\\le\\frac{6400p}{\\varepsilon},\n\\qquad\nD\\le1280\\left(\\sqrt{\\frac{dp}{\\varepsilon}}+1\\right),\n\\qquad\nD<\\min\\{p,k_0/2,k_1/2\\}.\n$$\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe active corpus contains no prior submission or verifier finding. Both campaign databases contain only metadata and job queues; every prior output and error field is null. All eight active leaderboards are empty arrays, and no submissions or review directories exist. Directories named `superseded` were excluded.\n\nThe benchmark is [KTZ Revision 1, Theorem 1.1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download): over every finite field, $\\varepsilon\\ge C(d/q)^{1/3}$ implies one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with global agreement at least $c\\varepsilon$. The bivariate proof gives the explicit value $c=1/8000$.\n\nThe exact bivariate chain used for comparison is KTZ Lemmas 3.1\u20133.2, 4.1\u20134.3, 5.1\u20135.2, and 6.1\u20136.3. The source-stated interpolation degree is $D=16(\\lfloor\\sqrt{d|\\mathcal R|}\\rfloor+1)$. The following exponent calculation is my reconstruction, not a quoted theorem: $|\\mathcal R|=O(p/\\varepsilon)$ and $N_d(D)=\\Theta(D^3/d)$, while every graph-line identity costs $O(D)$ coefficients. Hence $D^2\\asymp d|\\mathcal R|$ and\n\n$$\nD=O\\left(\\sqrt{\\frac{dp}{\\varepsilon}}\\right).\n$$\n\nBoth identity propagation and simple-root cleanup need $D=O(\\varepsilon p)$, producing $\\varepsilon^3\\gtrsim d/p$.\n\nFor historical comparison, [HKSS Theorem 4.2](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/182/download/) states that $q>Cd/\\varepsilon^7$ gives a bivariate polynomial with agreement $\\Omega(\\varepsilon^4)$. The exponent $1/7$ is obtained by rearranging that hypothesis; HKSS Theorem 1.4 itself leaves its exponent unspecified. HKSS Theorem 4.3 constructs an interpolant of weighted degree $O(d/\\varepsilon^2)$ and invokes Lemmas 2.9, 2.10, and 3.1 for separability and lifting.\n\nAn adversarial reading found two unresolved displayed transitions in the inspected HKSS version. Appendix Lemma A.2 assumes $r\\ge2\\log(q)/\\gamma^2$, whereas the later choice $r=900d/\\gamma^2$ checks this only when $\\log q\\le450d$. Separately, the proof of Theorem 4.2 establishes a mass parameter $\\mu=\\Omega(\\varepsilon^3)$ and later labels $\\mu q$ as $\\Omega(\\varepsilon^2q)$. I do not use either transition. These observations are audit cautions, not a declaration that the HKSS theorem is false; an omitted case split or revised accounting may repair them.\n\n## Theorem\n\n### Theorem 1: weighted resultant bound\n\nLet $U,V\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be nonzero and coprime. Let their weighted degrees be $u,v$ and their $Z$-degrees be $r,s$, with at least one of $r,s$ positive. Suppose $\\mathcal T$ is a family of distinct affine lines, each carrying $q_L(t)$ of degree at most $d$, such that\n\n$$\nU(L(t),q_L(t))\\equiv V(L(t),q_L(t))\\equiv0\n\\quad(L\\in\\mathcal T).\n$$\n\nThen\n\n$$\n|\\mathcal T|\n\\le su+rv-drs\n=\\frac{uv}{d}-\\frac{(u-dr)(v-ds)}d\n\\le\\frac{uv}{d},\n$$\n\nwith the evident direct interpretation if one $Z$-degree is zero. In particular, $|\\mathcal T|\\le\\lfloor uv/d\\rfloor$.\n\n### Theorem 2: prime-field interpolation and vertical cleanup\n\nLet\n\n$$\np\\text{ prime},\\qquad 101\\le d\\le p-1,\\qquad d\\le D<p.\n$$\n\nLet $\\mathcal R$ be $n$ distinct affine lines with degree-at-most-$d$ labels. If\n\n$$\nn>D,\n\\qquad\nN_d(D)>n(D+1),\n$$\n\nthere is a nonzero squarefree polynomial $A$ of weighted degree at most $D$ satisfying\n\n$$\nA(L(t),P_L(t))\\equiv0\\quad(L\\in\\mathcal R),\n\\qquad A_Z\\ne0.\n$$\n\nWrite $A=HB$, where $H\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the $Z$-content and $B$ is primitive in $Z$. For any family of graph lines on which $A$ vanishes formally:\n\n1. $B$ is squarefree and $\\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$.\n2. At most $\\lfloor D^2/d-D\\rfloor$ lines are either $H$-trivial or satisfy $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))\\equiv0$.\n3. Every remaining line has at most $D-d$ points with $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))=0$.\n4. Relative to uniform affine point-line incidences, deleting every such exceptional line and ramified point loses at most\n\n$$\n\\frac{D^2/d-D}{p(p+1)}+\\frac{D-d}{p}.\n$$\n\n### Corollary: component-sensitive lifting\n\nSuppose $B(b,\\alpha)=0$ and $B_Z(b,\\alpha)\\ne0$. Let $C$ be the unique irreducible factor of $B$ vanishing at $(b,\\alpha)$ and let $\\delta_C=\\operatorname{wdeg}C$. If more than $\\delta_C$ distinct lines through $b$ carry degree-at-most-$d$ roots through $\\alpha$, then a single total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q$ restricts to all those roots and\n\n$$\nC(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\\equiv0.\n$$\n\nIndeed, $C$ is associated to $Z-Q$. This refines the lifting threshold from the whole interpolant degree to the degree of the relevant component, though no worst-case bound forces $\\delta_C=o(D)$.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1 \u2014 proved: weighted Sylvester degree.]** Write\n\n$$\nU=\\sum_{i=0}^{r}a_i(X,Y)Z^i,\n\\qquad\nV=\\sum_{j=0}^{s}b_j(X,Y)Z^j.\n$$\n\nWeighted degree gives $\\deg a_i\\le u-di$ and $\\deg b_j\\le v-dj$. Every monomial in the Sylvester determinant contains $s$ coefficients of $U$, $r$ coefficients of $V$, and has total coefficient-index sum $rs$. The last identity also follows from\n\n$$\n\\operatorname{Res}_Z(U(TZ),V(TZ))\n=T^{rs}\\operatorname{Res}_Z(U,V).\n$$\n\nConsequently,\n\n$$\n\\deg_{X,Y}\\operatorname{Res}_Z(U,V)\\le su+rv-drs.\n$$\n\nNo ordinary-total-degree estimate is substituted here.\n\n**[P2 \u2014 proved: graph-line count.]** Coprimality makes the resultant nonzero. For each $L\\in\\mathcal T$, specialization to $\\mathbb F_p(t)$ gives the common root $q_L(t)$, so the resultant vanishes identically on the base line $L$. Its affine-linear equation therefore divides the resultant. Distinct lines give distinct linear factors, proving Theorem 1. If, say, $s=0$, then $V(L(t))\\equiv0$ directly and $|\\mathcal T|\\le\\deg V\\le v\\le uv/d$, since $r>0$ implies $u\\ge d$.\n\n**[P3 \u2014 proved: exact interpolation.]** For an unknown polynomial supported on the $N_d(D)$ weighted monomials, one graph-line identity has degree at most $D$ in $t$ and imposes at most $D+1$ homogeneous linear equations. The strict dimension inequality therefore supplies a nonzero $A$. If $A$ were independent of $Z$, it would vanish identically on $n>D$ base lines; their distinct linear equations would all divide a bivariate polynomial of degree at most $D$, an impossibility. Thus $A$ depends on $Z$. Since $D<p$, every positive $Z$-exponent is nonzero modulo $p$, so $A_Z\\ne0$.\n\n**[P4 \u2014 proved: squarefree primitive reduction.]** Choose $A$ of minimum weighted degree among nonzero graph interpolants. If $A=P^eR$ with $e\\ge2$ and $P\\nmid R$, then on each graph the product $P^eR$ is zero in the domain $\\mathbb F_p[t]$. Hence $PR$ is also zero there, but has smaller weighted degree and still depends on $Z$, a contradiction. Thus $A$ is squarefree. Dividing its coefficient content $H(X,Y)$ makes $B=A/H$ primitive in $Z$ and preserves squarefreeness. On any line not annihilated by $H$, the identity $A(L,P_L)=0$ implies $B(L,P_L)=0$ in the same domain.\n\n**[P5 \u2014 proved: vertical separability.]** Factor $B$ into distinct irreducibles. If an irreducible factor $C$ divided both $B$ and $B_Z$, squarefreeness would force $C_Z=0$. But $\\deg_ZC\\le\\deg_ZB\\le D/d<p$. In characteristic $p$, a polynomial of $Z$-degree below $p$ with zero $Z$-derivative is independent of $Z$. Such a factor would divide every coefficient of $B$, contradicting primitivity. Therefore $\\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. Absolute irreducibility is neither assumed nor needed.\n\n**[P6 \u2014 proved: ramification count and incidence loss.]** Put $\\delta=\\operatorname{wdeg}B$ and $r=\\deg_ZB$. Then $r<p$,\n\n$$\n\\operatorname{wdeg}B_Z\\le\\delta-d,\n\\qquad\n\\deg_ZB_Z=r-1.\n$$\n\nTheorem 1 applied to $B,B_Z$ bounds identically ramified graph lines by\n\n$$\n\\Delta=(2r-1)\\delta-dr^2\n=\\frac{\\delta^2}{d}-\\delta-\frac{(\\delta-dr)^2}{d}\n\\le\\frac{\\delta^2}{d}-\\delta.\n$$\n\nLet $a=\\operatorname{wdeg}A$ and $h=\\deg H$, so $a=h+\\delta\\le D$. Adding the at most $h$ content-trivial lines gives\n\n$$\nh+\\Delta\n\\le a-\\delta+\\frac{\\delta^2}{d}-\\delta\n\\le\\frac{a^2}{d}-a\n\\le\\frac{D^2}{d}-D.\n$$\n\nThe middle inequality follows because\n\n$$\n\\frac{a^2}{d}-a-\n\\left(a+\\frac{\\delta^2}{d}-2\\delta\\right)\n=(a-\\delta)\\left(\\frac{a+\\delta}{d}-2\\right)\\ge0.\n$$\n\nOn any other graph, $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $\\delta-d\\le D-d$, hence has at most $D-d$ roots. Exceptional lines contribute at most $p$ incidences apiece. Dividing by the total $p^2(p+1)$ incidences proves the claimed loss.\n\n**[P7 \u2014 proved: component-sensitive simple-root lift.]** At a point with $B_Z(b,\\alpha)\\ne0$, exactly one irreducible factor $C$ of $B$ vanishes, and $C_Z(b,\\alpha)\\ne0$. On every supplied graph through the point, the domain property forces this same factor, rather than another factor, to vanish identically. Newton recursion produces the unique total-degree-at-most-$d$ truncation $Q$ through $\\alpha$; it divides only by $C_Z(b,\\alpha)$. Its restriction equals every supplied $P_L$. Then $C(X,Y,Q)$ has degree at most $\\delta_C$ and vanishes on more than $\\delta_C$ distinct lines, so it is zero. The kernel of substitution $Z\\mapsto Q$ is $(Z-Q)$; irreducibility forces $C$ to be associated to $Z-Q$.\n\n**[P8 \u2014 conditional on the cited KTZ surrounding lemmas: application.]** Substitute the new cleanup for KTZ Section 5 while retaining their Lemmas 3.1\u20134.3 and 6.1\u20136.3. The new deletion bound is no larger than their Lemma 4.1 budget. The remaining graph therefore has the same minimum degree and incidence mass required for lifting and component propagation. Their conclusion supplies one polynomial $Q$ with\n\n$$\n\\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\\ge\\frac{\\varepsilon}{8000}.\n$$\n\nHowever,\n\n$$\n\\frac{D-d}{p}\n\\le O\\left(\\sqrt{\\frac{d}{\\varepsilon p}}+\\frac1p\\right).\n$$\n\nRequiring this to be $O(\\varepsilon)$ is equivalent, up to constants, to $\\varepsilon^3\\gtrsim d/p$. Thus this substitution does not improve Theorem 1.1's exponent.\n\n**[P9 \u2014 proved: uniform multiplicity barrier.]** Suppose a proposed point-interpolation proof imposes ambient Hasse multiplicity $s\\ge1$ at $M$ lifted points. The raw number of linear jet conditions is\n\n$$\nM\\binom{s+2}{3}.\n$$\n\nFor $D\\ge d\\ge101$,\n\n$$\n\\dim W_D=N_d(D)\\le\\frac{2D^3}{d},\n\\qquad\n\\binom{s+2}{3}\\ge\\frac{s^3}{6}.\n$$\n\nIf existence is certified by the standard raw coefficient inequality\n\n$$\nM\\binom{s+2}{3}<\\dim W_D,\n$$\n\nthen $(D/s)^3>Md/12$. If a target graph contains $k$ interpolated points, multiplicity root counting needs $sk>D$, hence\n\n$$\nk^3>\\frac{Md}{12}.\n$$\n\nFor $M\\ge\\rho p^2$ and $k\\le K\\varepsilon p$, this forces\n\n$$\n\\varepsilon^3>\\frac{\\rho}{12K^3}\\frac{d}{p}.\n$$\n\nThus uniform ambient multiplicity cannot improve the exponent through this coefficient-counting route. Dependent constraints, nonuniform multiplicities, or directional jets are not ruled out.\n\n**[P10 \u2014 refuted claim: higher Hasse order can replace simplicity.]** Take $p=409$, $d=101$, and\n\n$$\nB=Z^2-XY,\n\\qquad\n\\operatorname{wdeg}B=202<p.\n$$\n\nAt $(0,0,0)$, $B_Z=0$ while $\\partial_Z^{[2]}B=1$. For every projective direction $[a:b]$ with $ab$ a square, choose $c^2=ab$ and use $L(t)=(at,bt)$, $P_L(t)=ct$. There are\n\n$$\n2+\\frac{p-1}{2}=206>202\n$$\n\nsuch directions, and every graph satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))\\equiv0$. Nevertheless, $B(X,Y,Q)=0$ would give $Q^2=XY$, impossible because the exponent of the irreducible $X$ is odd on the right and even in a square. Hence even irreducibility, squarefreeness, generic separability, a nonzero second Hasse derivative, and more than $D$ pencil roots do not replace a fiberwise simple root.\n\n**[P11 \u2014 proved: exponent ceiling under uniform line sampling.]** Let $N=\\binom{d+2}{2}$ and suppose\n\n$$\nN\\log p<(4\\log4-3)p.\n$$\n\nFor uniformly random $f$, a fixed total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial agrees at a binomial number of points with mean $p$. Chernoff gives\n\n$$\n\\Pr[\\operatorname{agr}(f,Q)\\ge4/p]\n\\le e^{-(4\\log4-3)p}.\n$$\n\nA union bound over at most $p^N$ polynomials produces an $f$ with maximum global agreement below $4/p$. On each affine line, interpolate $f$ on any $d+1$ points. The resulting supplied line table has local agreement at least $(d+1)/p$. Taking, for example, growing $d=o(\\sqrt{p/\\log p})$ proves that any claimed exponent strictly larger than $1$ with global agreement $\\Omega(\\varepsilon)$ is false. This uses uniform affine-line sampling and total degree and does not obstruct exponent $1-o(1)$.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\nThe controlling calculation is\n\n$$\n|\\mathcal R|=O(p/\\varepsilon),\n\\quad\nD^3/d\\gtrsim |\\mathcal R|D,\n\\quad\nD=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\varepsilon}),\n\\quad\n(D-d)/p=O(\\varepsilon).\n$$\n\nTherefore\n\n$$\n\\sqrt{\\frac{d}{\\varepsilon p}}\\lesssim\\varepsilon\n\\iff\n\\varepsilon^3\\gtrsim\\frac dp.\n$$\n\nThe new exceptional-line term is only\n\n$$\n\\frac{D^2/d}{p^2}=O\\left(\\frac1{\\varepsilon p}\\right),\n$$\n\nwhere the ordinary-degree estimate was $D^2/p^2=O(d/(\\varepsilon p))$. This factor-$d$ improvement is not controlling.\n\nNo Markov loss occurs in the new proof. KTZ Lemma 3.2 uses a Chernoff estimate and a union bound over at most $p(p+1)$ lines, followed by Chebyshev for $|\\mathcal R|$; these introduce constants and the requirement $k_0\\gtrsim\\log p$, not another power of $\\varepsilon$. KTZ Lemma 2.1 is proved by Cauchy\u2013Schwarz and contributes $1/\\sqrt{p+1}$; Lemma 4.1 explicitly budgets it as at most $\\varepsilon/8000$. Under $\\varepsilon^3p\\gtrsim d$ and $d\\ge101$, it is not the controlling exponent. The second pruning loses only a constant fraction of $\\varepsilon$.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Adversarial random table:** [P11] rigorously proves the linear-scale floor and rules out exponents greater than $1$. It does not refute the campaign target.\n\n2. **Higher-Hasse lifting:** [P10] refutes the tempting replacement of simple roots by finite Hasse multiplicity. The failure already occurs at the campaign's lower boundary $d=101$.\n\n3. **Concentrated good directions:** choose $d+1$ distinct directions $u_i$ and linear forms $\\ell_i$ vanishing on them, and set\n\n   $$f(X,Y)=\\prod_{i=1}^{d+1}\\ell_i(X,Y).$$\n\n   On every affine line in direction $u_i$, the leading coefficient vanishes, so the restriction has degree at most $d$. Use that restriction as $P_L$ and use $P_L=0$ in all other directions. The exact local agreement is\n\n   $$\n   \\frac{(d+1)p^2+(p-d)((p-1)(d+1)+1)}{p^2(p+1)},\n   $$\n\n   while $Q=0$ has global agreement\n\n   $$\n   \\frac{1+(d+1)(p-1)}{p^2}.\n   $$\n\n   Both are $\\Theta(d/p)$ when $d=o(p)$. Thus good directions may be concentrated at the conjectured linear scale, but the example still has the required order of global agreement.\n\n4. **Inseparability:** $Z^p-X$ is primitive, irreducible, and squarefree as a multivariate polynomial, yet its ordinary $Z$-derivative is zero. Its weighted degree is at least $pd$, so it is excluded precisely by $D<p$. This confirms that the auxiliary degree condition is doing real characteristic work.\n\n5. **Near-$p$ regime:** if $d>p/2$ and $D<p$, then $\\deg_ZB=1$. For $d=p-1$, $D=d$ and $B_Z$ is constant. No inseparability obstruction appears; instead, the KTZ cubic hypothesis with a large absolute constant may simply be empty when $d/p$ is too close to one.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- All rings used for factorization are formal polynomial UFDs. Polynomial functions are never substituted for formal polynomials.\n- The only characteristic-sensitive implication is $C_Z=0$ and $\\deg_ZC<p$ implies $C$ is independent of $Z$.\n- Primitivity, not absolute irreducibility, excludes such a factor.\n- The resultant is not divided by a leading coefficient, so fibers where $\\deg_ZB$ drops are included in its zero set.\n- The simple-root Newton recursion divides only by the nonzero value $B_Z(b,\\alpha)$.\n- Hasse multiplicity in [P9] is defined through maximal-ideal powers, so no factorial denominators occur.\n- The substitution of a multiplicity-$s$ lifted point into a line graph produces a root of multiplicity at least $s$ because the lifted maximal ideal maps into $(t-t_0)$.\n- The $p=409$ pencil confirms that higher Hasse order does not give uniqueness.\n- At $p=103,d=101$, the exact dimension check shows failure of the raw interpolation inequalities, not failure of the theorem or a small-degree obstruction.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe result improves algebraic factor control but not the degree $D$ of the explainer. It therefore cannot by itself beat exponent $1/3$. The main surviving bottleneck is the need to spend up to $D-d$ bad roots on every nonexceptional line, together with the earlier need for more than $D$ accepted crossings to propagate the line identity.\n\nThe automatic vertical-separability argument requires the auxiliary interpolant degree $D<p$. It does not address a hypothetical construction with $D\\ge p$, and the example $Z^p-X$ shows why that extension is nonformal.\n\nThe multiplicity obstruction covers only uniform ambient multiplicity certified by the raw number of jet equations. It leaves open dependent node conditions, nonuniform multiplicity, component-specific interpolation, and directional jets.\n\nThe component-sensitive corollary helps only if one proves that the component supporting many accepted line graphs has weighted degree substantially below $D$; no such distribution theorem is proved here.\n\nFinally, finite-field arithmetic checks are used only for falsification and endpoint auditing. They do not establish the asymptotic soundness statement.",

research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0010/response.json:159:  "note_markdown": "# Popularity-sensitive core decoding and a bounded-star-energy obstruction\n\n## Abstract\n\nFix a prime field $F_p$, dimension $m=2$, and an integer $100<d<p$. I prove an asymmetric refinement of the accepted-component decoder. If an accepted subgraph has point minimum degree $u$, line minimum degree $v$, line measure $\u03c4$, and $w=min(u,v)$, then the two conditions\n\n$$\nuv \\ge 2^{60}dp,\n\\qquad\nuw^2 \\ge 2^{60}d\u03c4p^2\n$$\n\nforce one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial to agree with the point table on at least $v/(800p)$ of all points.\n\nFor the original accepted graph, let $u_*$ be the largest point-degree threshold supporting accepted-incidence mass at least $\u03b5/2$. The component theorem implies\n\n$$\nu_*\u03b5^2 \\ge 2^{70}d\n\\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad\nagr(f,Q) \\ge \u03b5/12800.\n$$\n\nThus a hypothesis $u_*\\ge \u03ba \u03b5^a p$ gives the conditional threshold $\u03b5\\ge(2^{70}/\u03ba)^{1/(a+2)}(d/p)^{1/(a+2)}$. This interpolates from exponent $1/3$ at the universally available scale $u_*=\u03a9(\u03b5p)$ to exponent $1/2$ when $u_*=\u03a9(p)$. It does not improve the unconditional benchmark.\n\nI also prove a template-popularity lemma and a complementary obstruction: for every fixed star order, diffuse modal-constant tables can have star energy only $O(\u03b5^s)$ while every degree-101 global polynomial has agreement $o(\u03b5)$. Consequently, a scale-free bounded-order collision-energy increment cannot supply the missing popularity.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nThere are $p^2$ points and $p(p+1)$ affine lines. Every point lies on $p+1$ lines and every line contains $p$ points. Each affine line $L$ carries a univariate polynomial $P_L$ of degree at most the ambient integer $d$, and $f:F_p^2\\to F_p$ is the point table. The sampling rule is exactly a uniformly random affine line followed by a uniformly random point on it; equivalently, it is a uniform affine incidence. Put\n\n$$\n\u03b5=Pr_{L,\\,x\\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)].\n$$\n\nThe accepted graph has edge $(x,L)$ exactly when $x\\in L$ and $P_L(x)=f(x)$. All global polynomials below have total degree at most $d$.\n\nFor a subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$, let\n\n$$\nt=|T|,\n\\qquad\n\u03c4=\\frac{t}{p(p+1)},\n$$\n\nand let $u$ and $v$ denote its point-side and line-side minimum degrees, respectively. For the full accepted graph, write $a_x$ for the accepted degree of $x$ and define the absolute upper-tail incidence mass\n\n$$\n\u03b4_j=\\frac{1}{p^2(p+1)}\\sum_{x:a_x\\ge j}a_x,\n\\qquad\nu_*=max\\{j\\in\\{1,\\ldots,p+1\\}:\u03b4_j\\ge \u03b5/2\\}.\n$$\n\nWhen $\u03b5>0$, this set is nonempty. Since points below $\u03b5(p+1)/2$ carry less than half of all accepted edges,\n\n$$\nu_*\\ge \\left\\lceil\\frac{\u03b5(p+1)}2\\right\\rceil.\n$$\n\nFor $s\\ge2$, $\u0393_s$ denotes the probability that $s$ ordered distinct uniformly sampled lines through a uniform point all accept there.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe exact benchmark is Theorem 1.1 of [Kominers--Thaler--Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, Revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/): over every finite field, $\u03b5\\ge C(d/p)^{1/3}$ implies one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with agreement at least $c\u03b5$. The following explanation of the exponent is my reconstruction, not a separately quoted theorem: their Lemma 3.2 gives $|R|=O(p/\u03b5)$, Lemma 2.2 gives an explainer degree $D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\u03b5})$, and identity extension and lifting require $D=O(\u03b5p)$. Hence $\u03b5^3=\u03a9(d/p)$.\n\nThe present proof uses KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.1--2.3, 2.5--2.7, 6.1, and 6.3. The local cached KTZ file is the earlier July 2026 version; theorem numbering is stable, but the revision above is the pinned source. The cached Arora--Sudan file is the STOC 1997 version rather than the Combinatorica 2003 article recorded in the bibliography, and no theorem-number transfer from that cache is used.\n\nThe durable corpus was audited through [DATA_MANIFEST.json](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/DATA_MANIFEST.json), all eight active campaign-10 submissions, their verifier audits, all active leaderboards, and the empty campaign-300 leaderboards; directories named `superseded` were excluded. The main reusable prior result is the verifier-accepted symmetric component theorem in [researcher-0002](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0002/note.md). The exact pair-collision and regular-carrier obstruction in [researcher-0008](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0008/note.md) shows that graph regularity alone gives no energy surplus. The verified singular-lift obstruction in [researcher-0006](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0006/note.md) remains relevant to any future factorwise refinement.\n\nFor historical comparison only, Theorem 4.2 of [Harsha--Kumar--Saptharishi--Sudan, arXiv v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12752) states the bivariate condition $p>Cd/\u03b5^7$. It is not used in the proof.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A (proved asymmetric core decoder).** Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, and let $G=(X,T,E)$ be a nonempty accepted subgraph. Suppose every $x\\in X$ has degree at least the integer $u$, every $L\\in T$ has degree at least the integer $v$, $\u03c4=|T|/[p(p+1)]$, and $w=min(u,v)$. If\n\n$$\nuv\\ge2^{60}dp,\n\\qquad\nuw^2\\ge2^{60}d\u03c4p^2,\n$$\n\nthen there is a single $Q\\in F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying\n\n$$\nPr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\\ge\\frac{v}{800p}.\n$$\n\nConnectedness of the input is not required.\n\n**Corollary B (proved implication; conditional exponent).** With $u_*$ defined above, if\n\n$$\nu_*\u03b5^2\\ge2^{70}d,\n$$\n\nthen some total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial satisfies $agr(f,Q)\\ge \u03b5/12800$. More generally, if $0\\le a\\le1$, $0<\u03ba\\le1$, and $u_*\\ge \u03ba \u03b5^a p$, then the conclusion holds whenever\n\n$$\n\u03b5\\ge\\left(\\frac{2^{70}}\u03ba\\right)^{1/(a+2)}\n       \\left(\\frac dp\\right)^{1/(a+2)}.\n$$\n\nThe exponent improvement for $a<1$ is conditional because no such popularity tail is known for every table.\n\n**Lemma C (proved template popularity).** Let $T_1,\\ldots,T_R$ be disjoint line families and let $Q_1,\\ldots,Q_R$ be total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials such that $P_L=Q_j|_L$ for $L\\in T_j$. Let $\u03c4_j=|T_j|/[p(p+1)]$, $\u03c4=\\sum_j\u03c4_j$, let $\u03b4>0$ be the normalized accepted-incidence mass on their union, and put $\u03b1=max_j agr(f,Q_j)$. Then\n\n$$\n\u03b4\\le \u03b1\u03c4+\\sqrt{\\frac{R\u03b1\u03c4}{p+1}}.\n$$\n\nIn particular, $R\\le\u03b4(p+1)$ implies $\u03b1\\ge\u03b4/4$.\n\n**Proposition D (proved bounded-star-energy obstruction).** Fix $S\\ge2$. For all sufficiently large primes $p$, at the legal ambient degree $d=101$ there is a deterministic table using constant line polynomials such that, for\n\n$$\nr=\\left\\lfloor\\frac{\\log p}{4\\log\\log p}\\right\\rfloor,\n$$\n\none has\n\n$$\n\\frac{r}{130p}\\le \u03b5\\le\\frac{26r}{p},\n\\qquad\nmax_{deg Q\\le101}agr(f,Q)<\\frac2p,\n$$\n\nand, simultaneously for $2\\le s\\le S$,\n\n$$\n\u0393_s\\le2^{s+2}(S-1)\u03b5^s.\n$$\n\nA fully explicit sufficient meaning of sufficiently large is obtained by setting $u_0=\\lceil4\\log p/\\log\\log p\\rceil$ and $v_0=\\lceil8\\log p/\\log\\log p\\rceil$ and requiring\n\n$$\nr\\ge133,\n\\quad r^2\\le p,\n\\quad p\\ge8r!,\n\\quad u_0+1\\le17r,\n\\quad v_0\\le33r,\n$$\n\n$$\n\\frac{2p}{(u_0+1)!}\\le1,\n\\quad\n\\frac{2p^3}{v_0!}\\le\\frac18,\n\\quad\np^{5253}(e/4)^p\\le\\frac18,\n\\quad\nS\\le p+1.\n$$\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1] (proved: asymmetric mixing).** Put $\u03be=|X|/p^2$, $\u03c1=|E|/[p^2(p+1)]$, $\u03b1_0=u/(p+1)$, $\u03b2_0=v/p$, and $\u03bb=(p+1)^{-1/2}$. Minimum degree and KTZ Lemma 2.1 give\n\n$$\n\u03b1_0\u03be\\le\u03c1,\n\\qquad\n\u03b2_0\u03c4\\le\u03c1,\n\\qquad\n\u03c1\\le\u03be\u03c4+\u03bb\\sqrt{\u03be\u03c4}.\n$$\n\nIf $\u03c4<\u03b1_0/4$, the first and third inequalities imply $\u03be<(16/9)\u03bb^2\u03c4/\u03b1_0^2$. Substitution into the third inequality and comparison with $\u03b2_0\u03c4\\le\u03c1$ give $\u03b1_0\u03b2_0<2\u03bb^2$, or $uv<2p$. This contradicts the first hypothesis. The symmetric calculation gives\n\n$$\n\u03c4\\ge\\frac{u}{4(p+1)},\n\\qquad\n\u03be\\ge\\frac{v}{4p}.\n$$\n\nThus $t\\ge up/4$. Substituting the line-measure bound into the second hypothesis yields\n\n$$\nw^2\\ge\\frac{2^{60}dp^2}{4(p+1)}\\ge2^{57}dp.\n$$\n\nThis last inequality, rather than an unstated fixed-$d$ assumption, supplies all logarithmic room below.\n\n**[P2] (proved: selector and probability losses).** The first hypothesis and $v\\le p$ give $u>8$. Select every line of $T$ independently with probability $8/u$. A point accepted on a target line $L$ is called reached only through a selected line in $R$ other than $L$. It has at least $u-1$ eligible lines, so its reach probability exceeds $3/4$. For distinct points of $L$, the eligible line sets are disjoint because two distinct points determine their unique common line, which is the excluded line $L$. Chernoff therefore bounds the probability that at most half of $N_G(L)$ is reached by $e^{-v/24}$.\n\nSince $v\\ge w\\ge\\sqrt{2^{57}dp}$, $2p^2e^{-v/24}<1/4$; this accounts explicitly for the union bound over all target lines. The sample-size mean is $8t/u\\ge2p$. Its lower- and upper-tail Chernoff bounds are respectively at most $e^{-p/4}$ and $e^{-2p/3}$. Hence some choice has\n\n$$\n\\frac{4t}{u}\\le r=|R|\\le\\frac{16t}{u}\n$$\n\nand reaches more than half of every line's accepted points. In particular, $r\\ge p$.\n\n**[P3] (proved: interpolation).** Set\n\n$$\nD=16(\\lfloor\\sqrt{dr}\\rfloor+1).\n$$\n\nThen $D^2>256dr$ and\n\n$$\nD^2\\le1024dr\n \\le2^{14}\\frac{dt}{u}\n \\le2^{15}\\frac{d\u03c4p^2}{u}\n \\le2^{-45}w^2.\n$$\n\nThus $D<w/5000$, $D<p$, and $r\\ge p>D$. KTZ Lemma 2.2 gives $dim V_D\\ge D^3/(64d)>r(D+1)$. Each formal identity on a selected line costs at most $D+1$ homogeneous conditions, so a nonzero candidate in $V_D$ exists. If it were Z-independent, KTZ Lemma 2.5 and $r>D$ would force it to vanish identically. Its allowed positive Z-exponents are not divisible by $p$, so its Z-derivative is nonzero.\n\nLet $S_R$ be the finite union of the selected polynomial graphs and choose a nonzero polynomial $A$ of minimum weighted degree among polynomials vanishing on $S_R$ with $A_Z\\ne0$. KTZ Lemma 2.3 makes $A$ squarefree. Its weight is at most $D<p$, so pointwise vanishing at all $p$ parameters on a selected line is a formal identity. This also explains why repeated-factor removal cannot lose the line identities.\n\n**[P4] (proved: identity extension).** Every $L\\in T$ has more than $v/2>D$ accepted points reached through a selected $M\\ne L$. At such a point,\n\n$$\nP_L(x)=f(x)=P_M(x),\n$$\n\nso $A(x,P_L(x))=0$. The restricted polynomial $A(L(t),P_L(t))$ has degree at most $D$ and more than $D$ roots; hence it vanishes formally. There is no Markov or multiplicity loss at this step.\n\n**[P5] (proved: prime-field simple-root cleanup).** Write $A=HB$, where $H(X,Y)$ is the gcd of the Z-coefficients of $A$. At most $D$ affine lines are contained in $H=0$. On every other line, division in the integral domain $F_p[t]$ gives $B(L(t),P_L(t))\\equiv0$. The polynomial $B$ is squarefree, Z-primitive, Z-dependent, and has degree below $p$.\n\nMoreover, $gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. Indeed, if an irreducible $C$ divided both, squarefreeness and reduction of $(CE)_Z$ modulo $C$ would give $C|C_Z$, hence $C_Z=0$. Since $deg_Z C<p$, this makes $C$ Z-independent, contradicting Z-primitivity. KTZ Lemma 2.6 now bounds the lines on whose graphs both $B$ and $B_Z$ vanish by $D(D-1)$. On every other line, $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $D$, so it has at most $D$ accepted roots. Thus at most\n\n$$\npD^2+Dt\n$$\n\naccepted edges are deleted. No discriminant or derivative is divided by.\n\n**[P6] (proved: asymmetric pruning).** Since $|E|\\ge vt$,\n\n$$\n\\frac{pD^2+Dt}{|E|}\n \\le\\frac Dv+\\frac{pD^2}{vt}\n \\le\\frac Dv+\\frac{2^{14}dp}{uv}\n <\\frac1{4000}.\n$$\n\nLet $u_1=\\lfloor u/100\\rfloor$ and $v_1=\\lfloor v/100\\rfloor$. Iteratively delete point vertices of current degree below $u_1$ and line vertices below $v_1$. This costs less than\n\n$$\nu_1|X|+v_1|T|\\le |E|/50.\n$$\n\nA nonempty graph remains. The hypotheses imply $u_1\\ge u/200$, $v_1\\ge v/200$, and $u_1,v_1>D$.\n\n**[P7] (proved: lift, propagate, recover measure).** Every surviving point is incident to an identity line and hence satisfies $B(x,f(x))=0$; retained edges also certify $B_Z(x,f(x))\\ne0$. At a point in any surviving connected component, more than $D$ incident line roots satisfy the hypotheses of KTZ Lemma 6.1. It produces one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q$ with $B(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\\equiv0$. The one-variable simple-root uniqueness used in KTZ Lemma 6.3 propagates this same $Q$ through the component.\n\nSince $u_1v_1\\ge uv/40000>2p$, [P1]'s asymmetric mixing calculation applied to this component gives point density at least\n\n$$\n\\frac{v_1}{4p}\\ge\\frac{v}{800p}.\n$$\n\nThe polynomial agrees with $f$ at every point of that component, proving Theorem A. There is no list-size or factor-count loss.\n\n**[P8] (conditional: popularity-tail translation).** Let $\u03b4_*=\u03b4_{u_*}\\ge\u03b5/2$ and retain all accepted edges incident to points of degree at least $u_*$. Their number is $E_*=\u03b4_*p^2(p+1)$. Peel point degrees below $U=\\lfloor u_*/2\\rfloor$ and line degrees below $V=\\lfloor\u03b4_*p/4\\rfloor$. Point deletions cost at most $E_*/2$, and line deletions cost at most\n\n$$\nVp(p+1)\\le E_*/4.\n$$\n\nThus a nonempty core remains. Under $u_*\u03b5^2\\ge2^{70}d$, floors give\n\n$$\nU\\ge u_*/3,\n\\qquad\nV\\ge\u03b4_*p/8\\ge\u03b5p/16,\n\\qquad\nmin(U,V)\\ge\u03b5p/16.\n$$\n\nConsequently,\n\n$$\nUV\\ge u_*\u03b5p/48>2^{60}dp\n$$\n\nand, for every component line measure $\u03c4_C\\le1$,\n\n$$\nUmin(U,V)^2\n \\ge u_*\u03b5^2p^2/768\n >2^{60}d\u03c4_Cp^2.\n$$\n\nTheorem A gives agreement at least $V/(800p)\\ge\u03b5/12800$. If $u_*\\ge\u03ba \u03b5^a p$, the displayed hypothesis follows from $\u03ba \u03b5^{a+2}p\\ge2^{70}d$. Universally $u_*\\ge\u03b5p/2$, so this recovers exponent $1/3$ with a large constant. For $a<1$ it is a genuine conditional improvement; $a=0$ gives exponent $1/2$.\n\n**[P9] (proved: template popularity).** Put $S_j=\\{x:Q_j(x)=f(x)\\}$ and $\u03b1_j=|S_j|/p^2$. The carried edges in $T_j$ are exactly the incidences between $S_j$ and $T_j$. KTZ Lemma 2.1 gives\n\n$$\n\u03b4\\le\\sum_j\u03b1_j\u03c4_j+\n\\frac1{\\sqrt{p+1}}\\sum_j\\sqrt{\u03b1_j\u03c4_j}.\n$$\n\nThe first term is at most $\u03b1\u03c4$. Cauchy--Schwarz, the only loss here, bounds the second sum by $\\sqrt{R\u03b1\u03c4}$. This proves Lemma C. If $R\\le\u03b4(p+1)$ and $\u03b1<\u03b4/4$, the two right-hand terms are below $\u03b4/4$ and $\u03b4/2$, a contradiction.\n\n**[P10] (proved: constant-label branch).** For constant-labelled lines, group by their constant value $a$. The sets $\\{x:f(x)=a\\}$ are disjoint, so Cauchy--Schwarz uses $\\sum_aPr[f=a]=1$ and removes the $R$ factor:\n\n$$\n\u03b4\\le \u03bc\u03c4+\\sqrt{\\frac{\u03c4}{p+1}},\n\\qquad\n\u03bc=max_aPr[f=a].\n$$\n\nThus $\u03b4\\ge2\\sqrt{\u03c4/(p+1)}$ implies $\u03bc\\ge\u03b4/(2\u03c4)\\ge\u03b4/2$. If constant lines carry at least a $\u03b8$ fraction of the total agreement, then $\u03b5\\ge2/[\u03b8\\sqrt{p+1}]$ already yields a constant global polynomial of agreement at least $\u03b8\u03b5/2$.\n\n**[P11] (proved: exact star moments).** For every deterministic table,\n\n$$\n\u0393_s=\\frac{1}{p^2(p+1)_s}\\sum_x(a_x)_s.\n$$\n\nThe integer sequence $(n)_s$ is discretely convex. If $\u03bc=\u03b5(p+1)=k+\u03b8$ with integer $k=\\lfloor \u03bc\\rfloor$ and $0\\le\u03b8<1$, convexity gives the sharp degree-only lower bound\n\n$$\n\u0393_s\\ge\n\\frac{(1-\u03b8)(k)_s+\u03b8(k+1)_s}{(p+1)_s}.\n$$\n\nFor $s=2$, expansion yields the exact identity\n\n$$\n\u0393_2=\u03b5^2-\\frac{\u03b5(1-\u03b5)}p+\n\\frac{Var_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)}.\n$$\n\nThus even perfectly regular accepted degrees supply only baseline collision energy $\u0398(\u03b5^2)$.\n\n**[P12] (proved: modal occupancy and concentration).** Choose every value $f(x)$ independently and uniformly. On each line choose uniformly among its modal values, using fresh independent line coins, and use that value as the constant polynomial $P_L$. Symmetric independent tie-breaking is essential; arbitrary deterministic tie-breaking need not give the claimed star identity.\n\nLet $M$ be the maximum occupancy when $p$ balls are thrown into $p$ bins and let $q=E[M]/p=E[\u03b5]$. If $Y$ counts bins of occupancy exactly $r$, the explicit conditions in Proposition D give\n\n$$\nE[Y]\\ge\\frac{p}{8r!}\\ge1,\n\\qquad\nE[Y^2]\\le E[Y]+\\frac{p^2}{(r!)^2}\\le65E[Y]^2.\n$$\n\nThe second-moment inequality gives $Pr[M\\ge r]\\ge1/65$, hence $q\\ge r/(65p)$. Conversely, $Pr[M\\ge s]\\le p/s!$, so the stated factorial condition gives $E[M]\\le u_0+1\\le17r$.\n\nChanging one point value changes maxima on only its $p+1$ incident lines and changes $\u03b5$ by at most $1/p^2$. McDiarmid therefore gives\n\n$$\nPr[|\u03b5-q|>q/2]\n \\le2exp(-q^2p^2/2)\n \\le2exp(-r^2/8450)\n \\le1/4.\n$$\n\n**[P13] (proved: simultaneous low energy and no decoder).** Fix a point and condition on its value. The punctured incident lines partition all other points. Their values and the independent tie coins are independent. Label symmetry and double counting the $M$ modal positions show that each incident line accepts the point with probability exactly $q$. Hence $a_x$ is conditionally binomial and $E[\u0393_s]=q^s$.\n\nMarkov at threshold $4(S-1)q^s$, followed by a union bound over $2\\le s\\le S$, fails with probability at most $1/4$. On $\u03b5\\ge q/2$, this gives $\u0393_s\\le2^{s+2}(S-1)\u03b5^s$.\n\nFor each fixed total-degree-at-most-101 polynomial $Q$, its agreement count with random $f$ is $Bin(p^2,1/p)$, so\n\n$$\nPr[agr(f,Q)\\ge2/p]\\le(e/4)^p.\n$$\n\nThere are $p^{5253}$ candidates because $(101+1)(101+2)/2=5253$. Their union-bound failure is at most $1/8$. The probability that any line has modal occupancy at least $v_0$ is at most $2p^3/v_0!\\le1/8$. All four bad-event probabilities total at most $3/4$, so a deterministic realization exists after freezing both $f$ and the tie coins. It has $r/(130p)\\le\u03b5\\le26r/p$, every line supports acceptance, every line accepts fewer than $v_0\\le33r$ points, the stated star bounds, and no global decoder of agreement $2/p$.\n\n**[P14] (refuted claim; obstruction proved).** Fix $s\\ge2$, $\u03b3>0$, and constants $c_0,c_1>0$. This directly handles irreducibility and inseparability; no generic derivative, discriminant division, or unverified separability assertion is needed. KTZ Lemma 2.6 applies its resultant only to this certified coprime pair. If a connected accepted-incidence subgraph has minimum degree $k$ and its line side occupies a fraction $\\tau$ of all affine lines, then a reaching family of size $O(\\tau p^2/k)$ suffices. The resulting trivariate explainer has weighted degree $D=O(\\sqrt{d\\tau p^2/k})$. Component-local accounting shows that the proof closes under\n\n$$\nk^3\\gg d\\tau p^2\\quad\\text{and}\\quad k^2\\gg dp,\n$$\n\nand yields one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with agreement $\\Omega(k/p)$. Thus a standard pruned component with $k=\\Theta(\\epsilon p)$ and $\\tau=O(\\epsilon)$ admits the conditional square-root threshold $\\epsilon=\\Omega((d/p)^{1/2})$, with global agreement $\\Omega(\\epsilon)$.\n\nThis does not improve the unconditional $1/3$ benchmark: no argument here forces the small-component hypothesis. Moreover, a balanced-color construction using constant line polynomials proves that a single family which covers half of every accepted line can genuinely require $\\Omega(p/\\epsilon)$ lines. Hence a further improvement must be a sparsify-or-decode argument, not a uniformly smaller graph-theoretic cover.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nFix a prime $p$ and an integer $100<d<p$; throughout $m=2$. There are $p(p+1)$ affine lines, each containing $p$ points, and every point lies on $p+1$ lines. Sampling a uniform line and then a uniform point on it is therefore the same as sampling a uniform incident pair.\n\nLet $f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p$, and let every affine line $L$ carry a polynomial $P_L$ of degree at most $d$. Put\n\n$$\n\\epsilon=\\Pr_{L,\\,x\\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)].\n$$\n\nThe accepted-incidence graph has an edge $(x,L)$ exactly when $x\\in L$ and $P_L(x)=f(x)$. For a subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$, write $k=\\operatorname{mindeg}(G)$, $t=|T|$, and\n\n$$\n\\tau=\\frac{t}{p(p+1)}.\n$$\n\nAll graph degrees below are accepted degrees, not ambient incidence degrees.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe active corpus contained no completed submission or verifier audit at the start and end of this run; every active verified, promising, rejected, and bottleneck leaderboard was `[]`. This was checked against [the durable manifest](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/DATA_MANIFEST.json) and both campaign databases, excluding every directory named `superseded`.\n\nThe quoted benchmark is Theorem 1.1 of [Kominers--Thaler--Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download): over every finite field, $\\epsilon\\ge C(d/p)^{1/3}$ implies a single total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with agreement at least $c\\epsilon$.\n\nThe explanation of the cubic exponent is my reconstruction from their proof, not a quoted theorem: Lemma 3.2 gives $|R|=O(p/\\epsilon)$; Lemmas 4.1--4.3 give $D=O(\\sqrt{d|R|})=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})$; and identity extension and later lifting require $D=O(\\epsilon p)$. Calling this an exponent-$1/7$ threshold is an algebraic rewrite of that displayed condition. With at least two good directions, the accepted graph is connected, has line measure $\\tau=\\epsilon$, and is governed by the planted polynomial.\n\nIndependent random tables accept with probability about $1/p$, far below the campaign range. When $d$ approaches $p$, both cube-root and square-root scales approach one, and the large-constant hypotheses become vacuous. No near-$p$ counterexample is claimed.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\nThe proof is entirely over the prime field and keeps $D<p$. Formal and functional identities cannot be confused for line polynomials because $d<p$. The eligible-monomial restriction ensures $A_Z\\ne0$. Squarefreeness and perfectness rule out an inseparable irreducible factor with all partial derivatives zero. The generic derivative is chosen over $\\mathbb F_p$ using fewer than $p$ exceptional hyperplanes. Resultants, rather than discriminant division, control common line roots. Newton lifting divides only by a certified nonzero simple-root derivative. Ordinary interpolation is used with no hidden multiplicities or Hasse-derivative assumptions.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe result does not prove that every accepted core contains a component with $\\tau=O(\\epsilon)$. A single connected component may have $\\tau$ close to one, in which case the new parameter law returns the cubic benchmark. The explicit constant $2^{40}$ is safe but intentionally very loose, making the finite nonvacuous range much smaller than the exponent notation suggests. Proposition C obstructs only a single cover required to work for every line; it does not obstruct an algebraically informed decoder or an adaptive localization argument. research_state/campaign-10-ultra/agent_logs/20260914T085605Z-05fbc9a6aa-63a2d46838/stderr.txt:205:  "note_markdown": "# Sharp incidence-only losses in bivariate prime-field line\u2013point agreement\n\n## Abstract\n\nFor the affine line-versus-point test on \\(\\mathbb F_p^2\\), I prove two exact incidence obstructions. First, for every prime \\(p\\) and every campaign degree \\(101\\le d<p\\), there is a deterministic legal table with local agreement \\(\\epsilon=d/p\\), accepted degree exactly \\(d\\) on every affine line, accepted degree \\(d\\) or \\(d+1\\) at every point, and acceptance supported on all lines. Any fractional family of lines that reaches a fixed fraction \\(\\theta\\) of the accepted points of every target line through *other* accepted lines has total weight \\(\\Theta(p/\\epsilon)\\), with a multiplicative gap at most \\((d+1)/(d-1)\\). Thus the \\(p/\\epsilon\\) scale cannot be improved by a universal graph-theoretic cover, even with exact near-regularity and fractional weights.\n\nSecond, for every table of agreement \\(\\epsilon\\), the probability that two uniformly chosen distinct lines through a uniform point are both accepted there is exactly\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon^2-\\frac{\\epsilon(1-\\epsilon)}p+\n\\frac{\\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)},\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(a_x\\) is the accepted degree of \\(x\\). The lower bound is attained by accepting exactly \\(k\\) direction classes. Hence the usual \\(\\epsilon^2\\) collision loss is sharp.\n\nBoth extremal tables have the obvious global polynomial \\(Q=0\\). They are therefore obstructions to incidence-blind proof architectures, not counterexamples to soundness. An exact primary-source audit also shows that KTZ already uses the affine Vinh estimate, while the stronger Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw bounds do not give the linear component size needed for global agreement in their characteristic ranges. The unconditional benchmark exponent remains \\(1/3\\).\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nFix a prime \\(p\\), an integer \\(101\\le d<p\\), and dimension \\(m=2\\). Let \\(\\mathcal L\\) be the \\(p(p+1)\\) affine lines of \\(\\mathbb F_p^2\\). Every line has \\(p\\) points and every point lies on \\(p+1\\) lines.\n\nA point table is \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\). Each \\(L\\in\\mathcal L\\) has one polynomial label \\(P_L\\) of degree at most \\(d\\), interpreted using a fixed affine parameterization of \\(L\\). Put\n\n\\[\nA(x,L)=1_{\\{P_L(x)=f(x)\\}},\\qquad\n\\epsilon=\\frac{\\sum_{x,L\\ni x}A(x,L)}{p^2(p+1)}.\n\\]\n\nThis is exactly uniform-line-then-uniform-point sampling. Let\n\n\\[\na_x=\\sum_{L\\ni x}A(x,L),\\qquad\nN_E(L)=\\{x\\in L:A(x,L)=1\\}.\n\\]\n\nFor nonnegative line weights \\(\\lambda=(\\lambda_M)_{M\\in\\mathcal L}\\), define the capped load reaching an accepted incidence \\((x,L)\\) through other lines by\n\n\\[\nu_{x,L}(\\lambda)=\n\\min\\left\\{1,\\sum_{\\substack{M\\ni x,\\,M\\ne L}}A(x,M)\\lambda_M\\right\\}.\n\\]\n\nFor \\(0<\\theta\\le1\\), call \\(\\lambda\\) \\(\\theta\\)-reaching if\n\n\\[\n\\sum_{x\\in N_E(L)}u_{x,L}(\\lambda)\\ge\\theta |N_E(L)|\n\\quad\\text{for every }L\\in\\mathcal L.\n\\]\n\nIndicator weights are ordinary selected-line families. Fractional weights also cover multisets after coincident copies are combined.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe active corpus contains four earlier submissions and four verifier audits. Researcher-0002 is the only accepted result: a connected accepted component of minimum degree \\(k\\) and line measure \\(\\tau\\) is decoded under \\(k^2\\ge2^{40}dp\\) and \\(k^3\\ge2^{40}d\\tau p^2\\), giving a conditional exponent \\(1/2\\) when \\(\\tau=O(\\epsilon)\\). Researcher-0001 is revise-grade: its support-sensitive cubic theorem and modal obstruction were validated, but its exact statement and mixing algebra need repairs. Researcher-0003 was rejected because its hashed theorem omitted essential hypotheses forcing a \\(Z\\)-dependent interpolant; its weighted-resultant lemma survives only with the fuller hypotheses in the note. Researcher-0004's exact jet count is revise-grade and shows only that uniform rank-blind multiplicity is exponent-neutral. No active submission proves an unconditional exponent above \\(1/3\\). The data manifest is a launch snapshot and is not current mathematical evidence; the live boards and audits control this synthesis.\n\nThe benchmark is [Kominers\u2013Thaler\u2013Zheng, Revision 1, Theorem 1.1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/): over every finite field, agreement \\(\\epsilon\\ge C(d/q)^{1/3}\\) yields one total-degree-at-most-\\(d\\) polynomial with global agreement \\(c\\epsilon\\). In its bivariate proof, Lemmas 6.2\u20136.3 give \\(\\epsilon/8000\\). The following explanation is a reconstruction, not a quoted theorem: Lemma 3.2 gives \\(|R|\\le6400p/\\epsilon\\); Section 4 uses \\(D=16(\\lfloor\\sqrt{d|R|}\\rfloor+1)\\); and Lemmas 4.1, 4.3, and 6.1 require \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\). Hence \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\). KTZ supplies one-sided bounds, not simultaneous \\(\\Theta\\)-saturation.\n\nThe exact affine spectral estimate already appears as KTZ Lemma 2.1. Its primary antecedent is [Vinh, Theorem 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0711.4427v1):\n\n\\[\nI(P,T)\\le\\frac{|P||T|}{p}+\\sqrt{p|P||T|}.\n\\]\n\nFor medium-size distinct sets, [Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw, Theorem 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.06284v4) proves\n\n\\[\nI(P,T)\\ll |P|^{11/15}|T|^{11/15}\n\\]\n\nonly when \\(|P|^{7/8}<|T|<|P|^{8/7}\\) and \\(|P|^{-2}|T|^{13}\\ll p^{15}\\). Their Theorem 4 additionally treats a genuine Cartesian set \\(A\\times B\\), under \\(|A|\\le|B|\\), \\(|A||B|^2\\le|T|^3\\), and \\(|A||T|\\ll p^2\\). These hypotheses cannot be silently imposed on accepted-point supports. Bourgain\u2013Katz\u2013Tao Theorem 6.2 has an unspecified gain depending on a fixed support exponent and is not used.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A (regular carrier and other-line fractional-cover obstruction).** Let \\(p\\) be prime and let \\(101\\le d<p\\). There exist \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\) and degree-exactly-\\(d\\) labels \\(P_L\\), one for every affine line, such that:\n\n1. \\(|N_E(L)|=d\\) for every \\(L\\), while \\(a_x\\in\\{d,d+1\\}\\) for every \\(x\\). Exactly \\(pd\\) points have degree \\(d+1\\), and the remaining \\(p(p-d)\\) points have degree \\(d\\).\n2. The agreement is \\(\\epsilon=d/p\\), and every affine line supports acceptance.\n3. For every \\(0<\\theta\\le1\\), if \\(\\operatorname{OPT}_\\theta\\) denotes the infimum of \\(\\sum_L\\lambda_L\\) over all nonnegative \\(\\theta\\)-reaching weights, then\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\theta p(p+1)}{d+1}\n\\le \\operatorname{OPT}_\\theta\n\\le \\frac{\\theta p(p+1)}{d-1}.\n\\]\n\n4. The total-degree-zero polynomial \\(Q=0\\) satisfies \\(Q(x)=f(x)\\) for every point.\n\n**Lemma B (exact two-line collision identity).** For any valid table in the same ambient regime, let \\(\\Gamma_2\\) be the probability that, after choosing \\(x\\) uniformly and an ordered pair \\((L,M)\\) of distinct lines through \\(x\\) uniformly, both \\((x,L)\\) and \\((x,M)\\) accept. Then\n\n\\[\n\\Gamma_2=\n\\epsilon^2-\\frac{\\epsilon(1-\\epsilon)}p+\n\\frac{\\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)}.\n\\]\n\nFor every integer \\(1\\le k\\le p+1\\), equality in the lower bound is attained by a valid table of ambient degree cap \\(d\\) with \\(\\epsilon=k/(p+1)\\).\n\n**Proposition C (black-box incidence range).** Let a balanced accepted component have \\(N\\) point vertices, \\(N\\) distinct line vertices, and minimum degree at least \\(k\\). If Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw Theorem 3 applies, then \\(N\\gg k^{15/7}\\). This consequence alone reaches \\(N=\\Omega(kp)\\) only outside that theorem's positive-characteristic range. If the point set is additionally a balanced Cartesian product and Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw Theorem 4 applies, its consequence \\(N\\gg k^{8/3}\\) likewise reaches \\(N=\\Omega(kp)\\) only outside its characteristic range.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1] (proved: affine incidence decomposition).** Add \\(p\\) dummy point vertices. For each \\(b\\in\\mathbb F_p\\), connect dummy vertex \\(z_b\\) to the \\(p\\) lines \\(y=mx+b\\), \\(m\\in\\mathbb F_p\\), and to the vertical line \\(x=b\\). The resulting bipartite graph has \\(p(p+1)\\) vertices on each side and is \\((p+1)\\)-regular. A regular bipartite graph has a perfect matching: for every left set \\(S\\), its \\((p+1)|S|\\) edges enter at most \\((p+1)|N(S)|\\) slots, so Hall's condition holds. Removing a perfect matching preserves regularity. Iteration decomposes the augmented graph into \\(p+1\\) perfect matchings, regarded as colors.\n\nAfter deleting the dummy edges, every real point sees every color exactly once. Every affine line misses exactly the color of its unique dummy edge. Each color is absent from exactly \\(p\\) affine lines because its perfect matching contains exactly one edge at each of the \\(p\\) dummy vertices.\n\n**[P2] (proved: select and repair colors).** Select any \\(d\\) colors and let \\(E_0\\) be their real incidence edges. Every point has \\(E_0\\)-degree \\(d\\). A line has degree \\(d\\) unless its missing color was selected, in which case it has degree \\(d-1\\). There are exactly \\(pd\\) distinct deficient lines.\n\nPut \\(r=p+1-d>0\\). In the graph of unselected real incidences from deficient lines to real points, every deficient line has degree \\(r\\), while every point has degree at most \\(r\\). Hence for every deficient-line set \\(S\\),\n\n\\[\nr|S|=e(S,N(S))\\le r|N(S)|.\n\\]\n\nHall gives a matching saturating all deficient lines. Add these matching edges to \\(E_0\\). Every line now has degree \\(d\\); the \\(pd\\) distinct matching endpoints have point degree \\(d+1\\), and all other points retain degree \\(d\\).\n\n**[P3] (proved: realize the accepted graph).** Set \\(f=0\\). For each fixed parameterization \\(L(t)\\), let \\(S_L\\subseteq\\mathbb F_p\\) be the \\(d\\) parameters of the selected edges on \\(L\\), and define\n\n\\[\np_L(t)=\\prod_{a\\in S_L}(t-a).\n\\]\n\nThis polynomial has degree exactly \\(d<p\\) and vanishes exactly on \\(S_L\\). Therefore the accepted-incidence graph is precisely the graph from [P2]. Since it has \\(p(p+1)d\\) edges out of \\(p^2(p+1)\\),\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon=d/p.\n\\]\n\nAll lines support acceptance. The legal global polynomial \\(Q=0\\) agrees with \\(f\\) everywhere.\n\n**[P4] (proved: fractional-cover lower bound).** Let \\(\\lambda\\) be \\(\\theta\\)-reaching and define the larger common capped load\n\n\\[\nv_x=\\min\\left\\{1,\\sum_{M\\ni x}A(x,M)\\lambda_M\\right\\}.\n\\]\n\nSince \\(u_{x,L}\\le v_x\\), double counting gives\n\n\\[\n\\theta d\\,p(p+1)\n\\le \\sum_L\\sum_{x\\in N_E(L)}u_{x,L}\n\\le \\sum_x a_xv_x\n\\le(d+1)\\sum_xv_x.\n\\]\n\nAlso\n\n\\[\n\\sum_xv_x\n\\le\\sum_x\\sum_{M\\ni x}A(x,M)\\lambda_M\n=d\\sum_M\\lambda_M.\n\\]\n\nThus\n\n\\[\n\\sum_M\\lambda_M\\ge\\frac{\\theta p(p+1)}{d+1}.\n\\]\n\nNo Markov, union, or Cauchy\u2013Schwarz loss occurs. An ordinary selected set is the special case \\(\\lambda_M\\in\\{0,1\\}\\), so the same lower bound applies to KTZ's stricter other-line reach condition.\n\n**[P5] (proved: fractional-cover upper bound).** Give every line weight \\(\\lambda_M=\\theta/(d-1)\\). At an accepted incidence \\((x,L)\\), at least \\(a_x-1\\ge d-1\\) other accepted lines pass through \\(x\\). Hence \\(u_{x,L}\\ge\\theta\\), so the weights are \\(\\theta\\)-reaching. Their total weight is \\(\\theta p(p+1)/(d-1)\\). This proves Theorem A, including a multiplicative upper-to-lower gap \\((d+1)/(d-1)\\le102/100\\).\n\n**[P6] (proved: collision identity).** For a fixed point \\(x\\), exactly \\(a_x(a_x-1)\\) ordered pairs of distinct incident lines are jointly accepted. Therefore\n\n\\[\n\\Gamma_2=\n\\frac{\\mathbb E_x[a_x(a_x-1)]}{p(p+1)}.\n\\]\n\nBecause \\(\\mathbb E_xa_x=(p+1)\\epsilon\\), expanding the variance gives\n\n\\[\n\\Gamma_2=\n\\frac{(p+1)^2\\epsilon^2-(p+1)\\epsilon+\\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)},\n\\]\n\nwhich is Lemma B. In particular, \\(\\Gamma_2\\ge\\epsilon^2-\\epsilon(1-\\epsilon)/p\\), and if \\(\\epsilon\\ge2/p\\), then \\(\\Gamma_2\\ge\\epsilon^2/2\\). This is one exact Jensen/variance loss and no further concentration loss.\n\n**[P7] (proved: collision equality and concentrated directions).** Fix \\(k\\) projective directions. Put \\(f=0\\), label every line in those directions by the zero polynomial, and every other line by the constant-one polynomial. These are legal labels under the ambient cap \\(d>100\\). Every point has accepted degree exactly \\(k\\), so the variance term vanishes. The agreement and collision probability are\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon=\\frac{k}{p+1},\\qquad\n\\Gamma_2=\\frac{k(k-1)}{p(p+1)}.\n\\]\n\nDirect substitution shows equality in Lemma B. The same \\(Q=0\\) has global agreement one, so concentrated directions sharpen the incidence loss but do not obstruct soundness.\n\n**[P8] (proved: where the KTZ cubic occurs).** KTZ Lemma 3.2 uses sampling rate \\(\\Theta(1/(\\epsilon p))\\), Chernoff plus a union bound over at most \\(p(p+1)\\) target lines, and Chebyshev for sample size. These estimates cost constants and produce only the one-sided upper bound \\(|R|=O(p/\\epsilon)\\). Weighted interpolation then gives\n\n\\[\nD=O\\left(\\sqrt{d|R|}\\right)\n =O\\left(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon}\\right).\n\\]\n\nThe distinct-root and lifting budgets require \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\). Squaring gives \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\). Theorem A shows that replacing the cover by a universally \\(o(p/\\epsilon)\\)-weight fractional cover is false, but does not rule out decoding the obstructing case before interpolation.\n\n**[P9] (proved: Vinh/KTZ mixing barrier).** KTZ Lemma 2.1 is the absolute affine form of Vinh's spectral estimate, with normalized error \\((p+1)^{-1/2}\\). Lemma 6.2 absorbs it using\n\n\\[\n(p+1)^{-1/2}\\le\\epsilon/8000.\n\\]\n\nAt the current cubic threshold this is weaker: \\((d/p)^{1/3}\\sqrt p=d^{1/3}p^{1/6}\\). For a prospective exponent \\(\\alpha>1/2\\), however, fix the legal lower boundary \\(d=101\\). If \\(\\epsilon=C(101/p)^\\alpha\\), then\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon\\sqrt p=C\\,101^\\alpha p^{1/2-\\alpha}\\longrightarrow0.\n\\]\n\nThus Vinh-only component recovery cannot establish linear global agreement in this regime. This is a method obstruction, not a counterexample to a stronger theorem.\n\n**[P10] (proved: Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw diagnostics).** In the balanced setting of Proposition C, minimum degree gives \\(kN\\le I(P,T)\\). Theorem 3 gives\n\n\\[\nkN\\ll N^{22/15},\\qquad N\\gg k^{15/7}.\n\\]\n\nFor this lower bound to be at least the required \\(kp\\), one needs \\(k^{8/7}\\gtrsim p\\), or \\(k\\gtrsim p^{7/8}\\). At that scale it forces \\(N\\gtrsim p^{15/8}\\), whereas the theorem's characteristic hypothesis in the balanced case is \\(N^{11}\\ll p^{15}\\), i.e. \\(N\\ll p^{15/11}\\). There is no asymptotic overlap.\n\nIf the balanced point set is genuinely Cartesian, Theorem 4 gives\n\n\\[\nkN\\ll N^{11/8}+N,\n\\qquad N\\gg k^{8/3}\n\\]\n\nonce the linear term is absorbed. Reaching \\(N\\gtrsim kp\\) would require \\(k\\gtrsim p^{3/5}\\) and hence \\(N\\gtrsim p^{8/5}\\). But the characteristic condition \\(|A||T|\\ll p^2\\), with \\(|A|=\\sqrt N\\) and \\(|T|=N\\), requires \\(N\\ll p^{4/3}\\). Again there is no overlap. These are exponent reconstructions from the quoted theorems, not source-stated low-degree-test conclusions.\n\n**[P11] (refuted: incidence-only shortcut).** The claim that acceptance density alone always yields either \\(\\omega(\\epsilon^2)\\) compatible line-pair density or an \\(o(p/\\epsilon)\\)-weight family reaching a fixed fraction of every accepted line is false. Lemma B refutes the first alternative and Theorem A refutes the second. Since both examples have a perfect decoder, they instead prove that a successful argument must branch on algebraic or value coherence.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| KTZ selection | \\(\\epsilon\\) | one inverse \\(\\epsilon\\) | \\(|R|=O(p/\\epsilon)\\) |\n| KTZ interpolation | \\(|R|\\) | square root | \\(D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\) |\n| KTZ root budget | \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\) | cubic comparison | \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\) |\n| Regular construction | degree \\(d\\) | none | \\(\\epsilon=d/p\\), line degree \\(d\\), point degree \\(d\\) or \\(d+1\\) |\n| Fractional reach | fraction \\(\\theta\\) | factor between \\(d-1\\) and \\(d+1\\) only | \\(\\operatorname{OPT}_\\theta=\\Theta(p/\\epsilon)\\) |\n| Collision extraction | \\(\\epsilon\\) | exact square plus finite correction | \\(\\Gamma_2\\ge\\epsilon^2-\\epsilon(1-\\epsilon)/p\\) |\n| KTZ/Vinh mixing | component degree \\(\\Theta(\\epsilon p)\\) | \\(p^{-1/2}\\) error | linear recovery only when \\(\\epsilon\\gtrsim p^{-1/2}\\) by this route |\n| Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw, balanced | minimum degree \\(k\\) | exponent \\(15/7\\) | \\(N\\gg k^{15/7}\\), insufficient for \\(N\\gg kp\\) in range |\n| Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw, Cartesian | minimum degree \\(k\\) | exponent \\(8/3\\) | \\(N\\gg k^{8/3}\\), insufficient for \\(N\\gg kp\\) in range |\n| Constructed global output | \\(f=0\\) | none | one \\(Q=0\\) with agreement \\(1\\) |\n\nThe new construction is deterministic. The only convexity loss is exposed exactly by the variance term in Lemma B. No logarithmic, Markov, union, derivative, or multiplicity loss is suppressed.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\nTheorem A is a successful counterexample to a universal smaller reaching family. Unlike the earlier random balanced-color example, it is deterministic, exactly regular on the line side, within one on the point side, supported on every line, valid at \\(d=101\\), and valid near \\(p\\). Its fractional formulation also prevents an apparent escape through line multiplicities or randomized weights.\n\nIt fails completely as a soundness counterexample: \\(f=Q=0\\) everywhere. This is the intended sparsify-or-decode separation. The earlier verifier-accepted balanced-color construction behaves similarly at larger local agreements.\n\nThe direction-class table attains the collision lower bound and tests concentrated good directions. It too has perfect global agreement. Thus neither high collision energy nor direction concentration alone identifies a hard instance.\n\nThe modal table from researcher-0001 remains the only active genuine endpoint obstruction: at ambient \\(d=101\\), it has local agreement \\(\\Theta(\\log p/(p\\log\\log p))\\) and global degree-101 agreement below \\(2/p\\). It refutes a literal constant-times-\\(d/p\\) theorem but stays below every fixed \\((d/p)^{1-\\eta}\\) trigger.\n\nInseparability does not enter either new construction. At \\(d=p-1\\), the regular construction remains valid, but its perfect global polynomial confirms that the near-\\(p\\) regime is not an obstruction.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The ambient field is exactly \\(\\mathbb F_p\\), and \\(101\\le d<p\\).\n- Each root polynomial has \\(d\\) distinct linear factors and formal degree below \\(p\\). Its zero set has exactly \\(d\\) points.\n- No derivative is divided by. The roots are simple, but simplicity is not used.\n- No discriminant, resultant, factor irreducibility, absolute irreducibility, or interpolation multiplicity is invoked.\n- Hall matching is proved directly by degree counting. No probabilistic method or finite computation proves existence.\n- Fixed affine parameterizations avoid division by a slope and treat vertical lines identically.\n- Lines are distinct geometric affine lines. Fractional weights are handled explicitly; source incidence theorems are not silently extended to multisets.\n- Constant labels in [P7] are legal under the fixed ambient cap \\(d>100\\); the excluded test parameter \\(d=0\\) is never studied.\n- At the lower boundary \\(p=103,d=101\\), the complement degree is three. At \\(d=p-1\\), it is two.\n- Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw's positive-characteristic inequalities are retained in [P10]; their implicit constants are not converted into an unstated explicit finite range.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe benchmark is not improved. Theorem A lives at the exact interpolation floor \\(\\epsilon=d/p\\), which is below every fixed-\\(\\eta\\) trigger when \\(d/p\\to0\\). It obstructs a proof module, not the target theorem.\n\nConnectivity of the regular accepted graph is not proved. The cover lower bound is global and remains valid regardless of its component decomposition. An algebra-aware algorithm may decode components separately, as \\(Q=0\\) demonstrates.\n\nLemma B controls only pair extraction from acceptance density. Additional polynomial information might distinguish its equality examples. Proposition C audits black-box unweighted incidence estimates only; it does not rule out a new weighted, lifted, or algebra-sensitive incidence theorem.\n\nThe Stevens\u2013de Zeeuw calculations assume balanced components, and the Cartesian calculation additionally assumes a true product set. General accepted components need not satisfy either shape hypothesis. Bourgain\u2013Katz\u2013Tao's fixed-support exponent is insufficiently explicit for the campaign's uniform \\(d,p\\) target and was not imported.\n\nAccordingly, improvement from exponent \\(1/3\\) toward \\(1/2\\) still requires a sparsify-or-decode or interpolation advance. First, for every prime \\(p\\) and every campaign degree \\(101\\le d<p\\), there is a deterministic legal table with local agreement \\(\\epsilon=d/p\\), accepted degree exactly \\(d\\) on every affine line, accepted degree \\(d\\) or \\(d+1\\) at every point, and acceptance supported on all lines.
